dial.summary: BTC Accumulation intact on Warsh's inaugural Jackson Hole keynote day (Aug 28): BTC at $80,294 (+2% on the day) with total crypto market cap $2.8T (+2.63%); BTC.D slipping to ~57.4% from 59% signals early altcoin momentum but has not sustained sub-55% to trigger Alt Rotation; funding at -0.0048% (slightly negative) remains the textbook accumulation signature—price rising while positioning neutral-to-short; macro broadly supportive with Global M2 expanding, ISM at a 4-year high (55.6%), curve steepening to +48bps, DXY at 99.18 (neutral band); real yields at 2.35% remain the key headwind; Warsh's 10:00 AM ET address (inflation at 3.4% vs. weak labor: July NFP -23K) is the decisive macro gate—neutral-to-dovish tone + soft September CPI (Sep 11) would green-light an ATH assault, hawkish pivot triggers Risk Off repositioning ahead of FOMC Sep 16.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: Global 4-bank M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) at ~$102.7T (latest available, ~6-week reporting lag; June 2026 data per MacroMicro); US M2 for July 2026 confirmed at $23,218B ($23.22T), 29th consecutive monthly increase, +6.11% YoY, record high; global M2 tracking ~$102.7T for June per MacroMicro 4-bank aggregate; no YoY contraction from any major central bank; 4-week uptrend confirmed; Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote (Aug 28) and September FOMC (Sep 16) are the next key catalysts for global liquidity trajectory; status supportive.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: July 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 55.6% (released August 3) remains the most recent reading—August 2026 data releases September 1 at 10:00 AM ET, the first post-Jackson Hole activity read; sub-indexes: New Orders 56.7%, Production 58.5%, Employment 52.8%, Prices Paid 71.1%; highest reading since May 2022; 4-week trend up (June 53.3% → July 55.6%, +2.3pp); status supportive (above 50 and rising; headwind thresholds of <48 falling or >62 not met; a September 1 collapse below 50 alongside a hawkish Warsh tone would trigger Risk Off reassessment).

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY at 99.18 on August 28, 2026 (up +0.07 from 99.11 on Aug 27; Barchart intraday shows 99.60 testing channel support below declining 200-day MA); 4-week trend down: DXY peaked near 101.64 in late July 2026 and has declined ~2.4% to 99.18, well above the 0.5% flat threshold; structural dollar weakness driven by US Treasury expanded long-term buyback program and rate cut expectations; status neutral (ICE DXY in 97.5–100 neutral band); Warsh's 10:00 AM ET Jackson Hole keynote (Aug 28) is the key directional catalyst—a hawkish tone sustains DXY above 100 (headwind), a neutral-to-dovish tone accelerates DXY toward or below 97.5 (supportive); NFP Sep 4 and CPI Sep 11 are the next decisive inputs.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: FRED DFII10 at 2.35% as of August 20, 2026 (H.15 released August 21; Aug 27 H.15 not accessible via proxy); 4-week trend down: ~2.43% (July 25) → 2.35% (Aug 20) = -8bps, down 3.7% over 3 months; inflation running at 3.4% (above 2% Fed target) per Jackson Hole preview data; status headwind (above the 2% absolute threshold despite the falling trend); a neutral-to-dovish Warsh keynote (Aug 28) and soft CPI (Sep 11) are the catalysts needed to compress real yields meaningfully below 2% ahead of FOMC Sep 16.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: August 28, 2026: 10Y yield at ~4.65% (stable since Aug 27; high of 4.75% Aug 21), 2Y yield at ~4.17% (Aug 25); spread = +48bps; confirmed 4-week steepening: ~+35bps (July 24) → ~+48bps (Aug 28) = +13bps, above the 5bps flat threshold; August 14 reading confirmed at +51bps before slight narrowing into late August; status supportive (positive spread AND sustained 4-week steepening trend intact); Warsh keynote (Aug 28), NFP (Sep 4), and CPI (Sep 11) are the next curve inputs ahead of FOMC Sep 16.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6,745,699M (~$6.745T) for week ending August 19, 2026 (H.4.1 released August 20); H.4.1 for week ending August 26 was released August 27 (not yet indexed via search); 4-week trend flat: ~$6.70T (August 5) → $6.745T (August 19) = +$45B (+0.7%), near flat threshold; August 12 H.4.1 showed ~$6.76T before modest pullback to $6.745T Aug 19, consistent with measured QT pace; balance sheet holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau with no aggressive QT signal; status supportive (holding flat; no overnight rate spike from QT; Warsh posture on QT pace is a key Jackson Hole watch item).

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate at -0.0048% on August 28, 2026 (per MacroMicro; slightly negative across major exchanges Binance, Bybit, OKX); BTC at $80,294 (+2% on the day) as total crypto market cap expands to $2.8T (+2.63%); slightly negative funding with price appreciation is textbook accumulation signature—longs not overextended, shorts mildly dominant; well below the +0.04%/8h overheating headwind threshold; 30-day trend flat: near zero throughout August vs elevated late-June/early-July levels; status supportive. (CoinGlass unreachable via proxy—value sourced from MacroMicro search result for Aug 28 2026.)

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$305B (CoinGecko Aug 28, 2026); total crypto market cap $2.8T (+2.63% on the day); stablecoin dominance 10.91% (essentially flat from 10.9% Aug 27; down from 11.06% Aug 26); BTC.D ~57.4% (slipping from 59% as altcoins outperform intraday); 30-day trend down: ~13-14% (July 26) → ~10.9% (Aug 28)—capital continues rotating from stablecoins into risk assets as BTC sustains $80K+ and alt momentum builds; status supportive (30-day falling trend confirmed; headwind condition—dominance rising while TOTAL rises—is opposite of current dynamics); BTC.D approaching but not yet breaking sub-55% threshold for confirmed Alt Rotation.

upcoming.title: Chicago PMI (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Chicago Business Barometer for August 2026 at 9:45 AM ET—released the last business day of August (Monday August 31); regional manufacturing cross-check against the July ISM surge (55.6%); a reading above 50 reinforces broad manufacturing expansion heading into the September 1 national ISM release and pre-FOMC September 15-16 positioning.

upcoming.title: ISM Manufacturing PMI (August 2026)
upcoming.note: ISM releases the August 2026 Manufacturing PMI Report on Business at 10:00 AM ET—first post-Jackson Hole activity read; July 2026 ISM at 55.6% (highest since May 2022); a sustained expansion above 50 reinforces risk asset positioning; a collapse below 50 alongside a hawkish Warsh tone would trigger a Risk Off reassessment; pre-FOMC September 15-16 positioning begins in earnest following NFP Sep 4 and CPI Sep 11.

upcoming.title: ADP National Employment Report (August 2026)
upcoming.note: ADP releases the August 2026 National Employment Report at 8:15 AM ET—private sector employment proxy arriving two days before the official NFP report (September 4); July ADP showed +44,000 private-sector jobs added; a weak reading would reinforce July NFP shock (-23K) and bolster the rate-cut case heading into FOMC September 15-16; a strong rebound toward +100K+ would complicate the dovish narrative.

upcoming.title: ISM Services PMI (August 2026)
upcoming.note: ISM releases the August 2026 Non-Manufacturing PMI at 10:00 AM ET—services sector counterpart to manufacturing ISM; services represent ~80% of US GDP; released one business day ahead of the August NFP report (September 4); a post-Jackson Hole services expansion reinforces the soft-landing narrative ahead of FOMC September 15-16.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended August 29, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending August 29—first post-Jackson Hole labor read; sets early framing ahead of the August NFP report (September 4) and FOMC September 15-16; a spike above 220K reinforces the case for a cut; a stable-to-declining read keeps the policy debate open heading into NFP.

upcoming.title: Nonfarm Payrolls (August 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Employment Situation for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET—the second-to-last major data point before FOMC September 15-16 (after CPI Sep 11); July 2026 NFP shocked at -23K (vs +79K forecast), ADP July +44K; a further contraction would strongly argue for a rate cut and would likely push DXY toward or below 97.5; a rebound toward +100K+ would complicate the dovish narrative; NFP and CPI Sep 11 form the trifecta (with Warsh's Jackson Hole address Aug 28) shaping the September FOMC decision.
